To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

early embryo lymphohematopotietic progenitors, when cultured with stromal cells and IL-7, generate long-lived, polyclonal, B-lineage cell populations capable of reconstituting adult immunodeficient recipients.

midgestation mouse embryonic stem cell lines can be established in long-term culture with stromal cell support and IL-7, and that these lines differentiate in vitro to B cells that can reconstitute the humoral immune system of immunodeficient mice.
B-lineage progenitors derived from early gestation mouse embryos can be established in vitro and reconstitute immunodeficient mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the establishment of a novel system for the in vitro generation and characterization of long-lived B cells from early mouse embryo progenitors.

the establishment and characterization of long-lived polyclonal cell lines derived from mid-gestation mouse embryo lymphohemopoietic progenitor cells, which spontaneously differentiate in vitro to CD 19(+)Igs(+) immature B cell and reconstitute immunodeficient mice in vivo.
the generation of B cells from early embryo progenitor cells and their subsequent in vivo repopulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
early embryo progenitors can give rise to long-term in vitro B-lineage cultures that are capable of reconstituting immunodeficient mice and generating specific humoral immune response.

early embryo-derived progenitor cells, when cultured with IL-7, are more sensitive than late gestation and mature bone marrow progenitor cells to in vitro IL-7-mediated differentiation and in vivo repopulation of the B cell lineage.

early embryo B progenitors are more sensitive to IL- 7-mediated signals than late fetal and adult progenitors and that early embryo B-lineage progenitors have a greater potential to spontaneously differentiate in vitro to B cells than their late fetal and adult counterparts, which is reflected by the ability of the early embryo-derived cell lines to repopulate adult immunodeficient recipients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the early embryo B-cell progenitors are more immature, and thus more dependent on IL-7 for their in vitro establishment, than those progenitors obtained later in gestation or in the adult, and that the early embryo-derived B-cell progenitors have a greater in vivo repopulation potential.

midgestation embryo progenitors are highly sensitive to IL7-mediated signals, and the early embryo B-cell progenitors are more sensitive to IL- 7-mediated signals for their differentiation in vitro, and that the early B-lineage cells generated in vitro are capable of repopulating adult mice and of generating humoral immune responses.
early embryo-derived lymphohematopoiesis is highly dependent upon the cytokine milieu and that the in vivo reconstitution of adult mice with early embryo-derived B cells is highly efficient.
The main takeaway from our work is that

early embryo lymphohematopoeitic progenitors can be used to reconstitute immunodeficient mice and that these progenitors have a unique potential for in vitro B-cell differentiation in the presence of IL-7 that is not observed with progenitors from late gestation or adult animals.
early B-lineage progenitors from mouse embryos are highly sensitive to IL7 signals, and their in vitro establishment requires the use of IL-7 in combination with stromal cells.

early embryo-derived lymphohematopoetic progenitor cells are more sensitive to IL- 7-mediated signals than those derived from late gestation fetal liver and adult bone marrow, and that the early embryo-derived progenitor cells can be used as a model system to study early B-lymphocyte development.
